education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 6289 -1971 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

STAPLE, EPIPHYSEAL, ORTHOPAEDIC 



( Reaffirmed 2002 ) 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements for staple used for epiphyseal arrest in orthopaedic 
surgery. 

2. Material — Any one of the four materials specified in 3 of IS : 5347-1 969 ' Specification for general 
requirements of metal surgical implants' shall be used. 



3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 1 STAPLE, EPIPHYSEAL, ORTHOPAEDIC 

4. Workmanship and Finish — The staple shall be symmetrical having parallel arms with sharp-pointed 
ends. It shall be free from cracks, draw marks, pits, burrs, surface contamination and impregnated 
foreign particles. It shall be passivated and polished bright to give a mirror or satin finish. 

5. Tests 

5.1 Corrosion Resistance Test — As prescribed in 6.1.1 of IS : 5347-1 969. 

5.2 Performance Test — One arm of the staple shall be held in a suitable vice and a load of 200 N 
( 20 kgf approximately ) for 2'24 mm diameter staple and 150 N (15 kgf approximately ) for 1'60 mm 
diameter staple shall be applied on the other arm at its tip through a spring balance. The test shall be 
repeated with the other arm in the vice. The two arms of the staple shall remain parallel after the test. 

6. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. However, it is recommended that 
each staple or a suitable number of staples of the same size and material should be kept in a polyethylene 
bag or wrapped in wax paper and then a suitable number of such pieces packed in a carton. 

7. Marking — Each packet shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark; and the 
size and material of the staples. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi 1. 



Adopted 15 October 1971
